key_concepts: Matter is anything that has weight and occupies space.
Matter can exist as solid, liquid, or gas.
Solids have their own shape and can be held.
Solid molecules are tightly packed and move only slightly.
Solids can be described by color, shape, size, texture, weight, and volume.
Common solid shapes include round, oval, triangle, rectangle, and square.
Texture describes the surface quality of a solid, such as smooth, rough, soft, or hard.
Weight is measured with a weighing scale using kilograms or grams.
Volume is the space an object occupies and can be computed as length x width x height.
Examples of solids include ball, key, wood, table, crayon, book, and pencil.
Water, air, juice, and clouds are not solids.
